title: Playing at The Bushwick Starr until May 16th only!! #theatre #immersi...
transcript: it's like interactive theatre meets elementary school nostalgia in this whimsical theatrical experience set in a cartoonish laboratory each audience member receives a collection of props including but not limited to a notebook and writing utensils a balloon and a book underneath your seat the show is called Have You Ever Thought About created and performed by Michael Oluokun In which they conduct a series of exercises and performance segments to explain their scientific theory of “thinking about” some of that is just their own personal musings on the world but there's also a lot of audience participation sometimes as a group and sometimes with individuals on a volunteer basis like at one point I volunteered to throw some darts at a dartboard at other points we're given space to work on our own little solo projects very reminiscent of grade school and all in service of the science of “thinking about” but what they actually mean by “thinking about” is a little bit elusive a lot of the show… how should I say this? …kind of reminded me of conversations I might have had with my friends when I accidentally ate a whole gummy instead of half but as best I could tell it has a lot to do with metacognition and giving our minds permission to wander to new places and that's definitely reflected in the sometimes relaxed Loosy-Goosey feel to the show which I admit I struggled with at first until I realized that it went both ways allowing you to engage or disengage on your own terms like a few times I was more interested in my notebook doodles than what was happening on stage and yet both were valid ways to experience the show although the novelty combined with the slightly perplexing premise sometimes made it tough for me to absorb what was happening underneath the show takes a more serious turn at the end and I think I kind of understood how it tied things together like the mind expansion idea being a way for Oluokun to feel more seen and understood in a world where they don't fit into neat boxes but in other ways Oluokun frames the tonal shift in a way that feels a bit at odds with itself as if to say “that was the goofy part and here's the serious part” rather than saying “here's why the goofiness actually mattered” but it's also possible that I just didn't really understand it and yet I had a really good time with it anyway
classificationReason: Creator attended interactive show at The Bushwick Starr and shares direct opinions on the experience, but 'Have You Ever Thought About' is not on the provided list.
